questions.stem: In a queue of 41 candidates, a candidate is 16th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 22. New front rank = 16+4 = 20. Back rank = 41 − 20 + 1 = 22.

questions.stem: In a queue of 54 candidates, a candidate is 16th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. New front rank = 16+3 = 19. Back rank = 54 − 19 + 1 = 36.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 32 km north, turns left and walks 36 km, then turns left and walks 5 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 27 km along the initial direction and 36 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(27² + 36²) = 45 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 60 km west, turns left and walks 75 km, then turns left and walks 20 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 85. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 40 km along the initial direction and 75 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(40² + 75²) = 85 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 57 km east, turns right and walks 48 km, then turns right and walks 21 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 36 km along the initial direction and 48 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(36² + 48²) = 60 km.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
digital savings rural = vo pa to
digital secure credit = to re mi
savings secure access = ze re pa
rural credit access = mi ze vo
digital savings access = pa to ze
What is the code for “digital”?
questions.explanation: Answer: to. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: digital = to, savings = pa, rural = vo, secure = re, credit = mi, access = ze.

questions.stem:
Statements: X = P < R < S = U.
Conclusions: I. P < U   II. U ≤ R.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem: D is the only daughter of F. F is the father of D. B is the son of D. E is the sister of F. How is F related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of D, and D is B’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: B is the mother of C. H is the son of C. D is the father of C. How is H related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. D is a parent of C, and H is C’s son. Hence H is D’s grandchild.

questions.stem: B is the brother of D. D is the mother of H. A is the father of B and D. How is B related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. B is the brother of H’s mother D. Therefore B is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem:

I. Some notes are deposits.
II. Some files are tokens.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few notes are files. Some files are deposits. All deposits are tokens.
Conclusions:
I. All notes are tokens.
II. No files is a tokens.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few notes are files. All files are deposits. No deposits is a tokens.
Conclusions:
I. Some notes are not files.
II. No files is a tokens.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No notes is a files. Some files are deposits. All deposits are tokens.
Conclusions:
I. All notes are tokens.
II. Some tokens are files.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.
